entities.name: Jayasimha Siddharaja
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jayasiṃha, who assumed the title Siddharāja, ruled the Kingdom of Gujarat between 1092 and 1142. He was a member of the Chaulukya dynasty.

Jayasiṃha's reign was marked by significant military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, including the Kakatiya Empire. He also oversaw the construction of several temples and the development of trade with neighboring regions.

Jayasiṃha's legacy can be seen in the continued prosperity of the Kingdom of Gujarat under his successors. The Chaulukya dynasty continued to play a significant role in regional politics and trade for centuries after his death.

The inscription on the famous Bhimbawada Pillar, erected during Jayasiṃha's reign, bears a poignant message: 'Let the kings of India be aware of the rule of Jayasiṃha, who was a just and wise ruler, and who fought for the welfare of the people.'
